channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan Railway to Boost Eurasian Trade Hub Status
item.description: The construction of the China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway is a key development for Central Asia, according to Mukhtor Umarov, Chairman of the Uzbekistan Economic Assembly. He stated this initiative, linked with the Middle Corridor and the Trans-Afghan route, will significantly shorten logistics and position Uzbekistan as a crucial Eurasian trade node.

item.title: Biosecurity and Zoonotic Diseases Key Concerns in Central Asia, Expert Says
item.description: Kairat Tabyanov, a virologist and biosecurity specialist at the Regional Environmental Center for Central Asia (CAREC), highlighted the growing importance of biosecurity in Central Asia due to global changes and trade. He focuses on zoonoses, infections transmissible from animals to humans, and consults on a World Bank project for the veterinary sector.

item.title: One Health Approach Crucial for Central Asia's Economic Growth and Health Security
item.description: Pierre Gerber, a senior agricultural economist at the World Bank, emphasized the need for a 'One Health' approach in Central Asia to balance economic opportunities with health and ecosystem security. He spoke at a regional conference in Bishkek aimed at strengthening intersectoral cooperation and accelerating project implementation for this initiative.

item.title: Uzbekistan plans to establish Biome Center in collaboration with South Korea
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to establish a Biome Center in collaboration with South Korea, following a memorandum signed in Seoul. The center, originating from the Academy of Sciences' Center for Advanced Technologies, will create world-class infrastructure for cell technology research and application.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Oman to Jointly Confront Environmental Challenges
item.description: Uzbekistan and Oman held a meeting during Oman Climate Week to discuss expanding cooperation on climate change and environmental protection. Both nations face shared issues like water scarcity and desertification. Uzbekistan is interested in Oman's desalination and water management expertise.

item.title: Uzbek President Meets Compatriots in South Korea During State Visit
item.description: During his state visit to South Korea, President Shavkat Mirziyoyev met with Uzbek citizens working and studying there. Discussions focused on reforms in Uzbekistan and proposals for strengthening economic, scientific, and educational ties. Emphasis was placed on integrating AI and Korean digital technologies into Uzbekistan's economy and governance.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Build $100 Million Waste-to-Energy Plant in Khorezm
item.description: A $100 million waste-to-energy plant is planned for construction in Uzbekistan's Khorezm region. South Korean company Green Hammer Co., Ltd. will invest in the facility, designed to process 800 tons of waste daily and generate 71 million kWh of electricity annually. The project is scheduled for implementation between 2026 and 2028.

item.title: Uzbekistan and South Korea: Strategic Partnership Figures Highlight Trade Imbalance
item.description: Trade between Uzbekistan and South Korea reached $1.1 billion in January-July, with Uzbekistan's exports at $37.5 million and imports from South Korea at $1.037 billion. This imbalance is attributed to Uzbekistan's demand for high-tech equipment. South Korea invested $216.4 million in Uzbekistan during January-June, with 730 Korean-capitalized enterprises operating in the country.

item.title: Uzbekistan President Discusses Airport Cooperation with South Korean Firm
item.description: Uzbekistan's President Shavkat Mirziyoyev met with Kim Beom Ho, acting president of Incheon International Airport Corporation, in South Korea. They discussed modernizing Urgench airport and building a new Tashkent airport. The Korean firm plans to open an office in Tashkent, potentially becoming a center for airport management and training.

item.title: Uzbekistan Proposes Gradual Increase in Retirement Age
item.description: Uzbekistan's Ministry of Economy and Finance has proposed gradually increasing the retirement age from 60 to 63 for men and from 55 to 58 for women. The plan involves a three-month annual increase starting in 2028, aiming for completion by 2039. The proposal is currently open for public discussion until September 30.

item.title: Tax Committee Generated 72% of Uzbekistan's Budget Revenue in H1 2026
item.description: Uzbekistan's Tax Committee generated 72% of the state budget revenue in the first half of 2026, totaling 149 trillion soms. Overall budget revenues reached 277 trillion soms, a 63 trillion increase year-on-year. Customs Committee contributed 20% of the revenue. Corporate income tax revenue surged 2.3 times.

item.title: Uzbekistan Allocates 229 Billion Soms for Child Vaccinations in First Half of 2026
item.description: Uzbekistan spent approximately 23 trillion soms on healthcare in the first six months of 2026. Of this, 229 billion soms were allocated for child vaccinations, immunizing 1.4 million children against 13 infectious diseases. Significant funds also went to medical staff salaries, medicines, and hospital construction/renovation.

item.title: Karakol Municipal Fleet Expands with 63 New Buses
item.description: Karakol has introduced new modern buses equipped with air conditioning for its city and suburban routes. The mayor inspected the transport, which currently includes over 50 buses serving 15 lines. An additional 63 buses will join the fleet, enhancing public transportation for 10-12 thousand daily passengers.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Interior Ministry Investigates Charity Fund for Alleged Fraud
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Interior Ministry is investigating a criminal case of fraud against the charity fund 'Biz el menen.' The fund's leader and founders are suspected of collecting large sums of money through bank accounts, with preliminary damages estimated at 30 million soms between 2024-2026. The fund's leader has been detained.

item.title: Kyrgyz Students at GITIS Face Housing Issues; Ministry of Culture Intervenes
item.description: Kyrgyz students studying at the Russian Institute of Theatre Arts (GITIS) are facing housing problems due to dormitory repairs. The Ministry of Culture is working to resolve the issue and ensure suitable living conditions for the students, with the matter under the personal control of the minister.

item.title: Pregnant Woman Dies in Surxondaryo Due to Negligence of Surgeons
item.description: A pregnant woman died in Surxondaryo due to the negligence of surgeons. She had visited doctors twice, receiving different diagnoses, but intestinal obstruction was not identified. Her condition worsened, leading to her death and that of her fetus.

item.title: Tajikistan-South Korea Cooperation in Mining and Digitalization Discussed
item.description: South Korea and Central Asian countries plan to develop cooperation in mining and digitalization of production. Tajik President Emomali Rahmon arrived in Seoul to participate in the Central Asia-Korea Forum. Over 2 million Tajik tourists visited Uzbekistan in eight months.

item.title: Kyrgyz President Sapar Japarov Arrives in South Korea for Official Visit
item.description: Kyrgyz President Sapar Japarov has arrived in the Republic of Korea for an official visit. He was welcomed at the airport by South Korea's First Vice Minister of Climate, Energy, and Environment Kim Han-seung. The visit includes bilateral meetings with South Korean leadership and participation in the first 'Central Asia + Republic of Korea' summit.

item.title: Audit Chamber: $25 Million State Loan Issued Ineffectively to Company Linked to Tashiev
item.description: The Audit Chamber stated that the state "ineffectively" issued a $25 million loan to a fuel company associated with former GKNB head Kamchybek Tashiev. The firm belongs to Akylbek Mamatov, whose family has won state tenders for fuel supply for 10 years.

item.title: Patrushev Responds to Polish Minister's Statement on Defeating Russia
item.description: Nikolai Patrushev, an aide to Russian President Putin, sharply responded to a statement by the Polish Foreign Minister regarding the defeat of Russia. Patrushev stated that if a military conflict arises, all available capabilities would be used against Poland, suggesting Poland would be destroyed in two to three days.

item.title: Kyrgyz Students in Astana Apologize for Remarks on Kazakh History
item.description: Two Kyrgyz students studying in Astana on an exchange program have apologized for their statements regarding the history of the Kazakh people. Their apology came after a video circulated on social media showing them discussing the origins of Kyrgyz and Kazakh peoples and historical events, including controversial remarks about Kenesary Khan's head.

item.title: Uzbekistan Plans Airport Management Competence Center with South Korean Operator
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to establish an airport management, digitalization, and training competence center in Tashkent. This initiative follows a meeting between President Mirziyoyev and Incheon International Airport Corporation (IIAC) officials. IIAC is already involved in modernizing Urgench airport and constructing a new Tashkent international airport.

item.title: Uzbekneftgaz Prepares for Winter: Crucial 30 Days Begin for Gas Supply
item.description: Uzbekneftgaz is entering a critical 30-day period to prepare for the upcoming winter season and ensure stable natural gas supply to consumers. Chairman Abdugani Sanginov emphasized the urgency, stating, 'Winter is approaching, and our people need gas.' The company is analyzing measures to guarantee consistent gas provision.

item.title: Uzbek President Meets Compatriots in South Korea, Expresses Gratitude
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev met with Uzbek citizens in South Korea, thanking them for their contributions to the country's socio-economic development. He emphasized that their initiatives will be thoroughly studied and supported. Further details are available via the provided link.

item.title: IAEA Predicts Global Nuclear Power Capacity to Triple by 2060
item.description: The International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) forecasts global nuclear power capacity will triple by 2060. Countries are increasingly using nuclear energy for electricity demand and energy security. Small modular reactors are seen as a key source of clean energy. Central and Eastern Asia are expected to see the largest growth in nuclear capacity.

item.title: Incheon Airport Corporation Plans to Open Representative Office in Tashkent
item.description: Incheon Airport Corporation is planning to open a representative office in Tashkent. Additionally, a master plan will be developed for the development of the area around the new airport. Further details are available via the provided link.

item.title: Uzbekistan Expands Criminal Liability for Interfering with Investigations and Court Cases
item.description: Uzbekistan has expanded criminal liability for interfering with investigations and court proceedings. President Shavkat Mirziyoyev signed a law clarifying penalties for influencing investigators, prosecutors, and judges. The law also broadens administrative liability for contempt of court and takes effect September 12.

item.title: Uzbek President Attends Uzbek-Korean Business Forum, Proposes Joint Economic Growth Initiatives
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev and South Korean Prime Minister Han Duck-soo participated in an Uzbek-Korean business forum in Tashkent. Over 300 representatives from government and business attended. President Mirziyoyev highlighted Korea as a strategic partner and proposed combining resources, technology, and capital for new economic growth points.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's mining potential presented to British businesses in Bishkek
item.description: British companies learned about Kyrgyzstan's investment climate and mining sector changes at a meeting in Bishkek. UK engineering and consulting firms offered solutions in exploration, processing, and environmental safety. Experts discussed the country's mineral resources and licensing, noting a significant increase in foreign investment in mining.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Mining Sector Potential Presented to British Businesses
item.description: Representatives from British companies were informed about Kyrgyzstan's investment climate and recent developments in its mining industry. The International Business Council (IBC) reported that the meeting, organized by the British Embassy, covered geological exploration, mineral processing, and environmental safety. Foreign direct investment in mining increased significantly.

item.title: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov arrives in South Korea for official visit
item.description: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov arrived in South Korea for an official visit, where he was met by high-ranking officials. He is scheduled to hold bilateral meetings with Korean leadership and attend the first Central Asia-Republic of Korea summit, as well as a business summit session.

item.title: Tajikistan seeks investment for new solar power plants, discusses with China's LONGi
item.description: Tajikistan is seeking investment for the construction of new solar power plants. To this end, the country has discussed potential investment in this sector with China's LONGi company. Further details are expected.

item.title: Youth employment and career guidance event held in Namangan region
item.description: An event focused on youth career guidance and employment was held at Vocational School No. 2 in the Naryn district of Namangan region. The event included an open dialogue with young people studying professions like sewing, plumbing, and IT. Officials emphasized quality training and job placement.

item.title: Uzbekistan proposes reduced working hours for older employees starting 2027
item.description: Uzbekistan proposes introducing reduced working hours for women over 55 and men over 60, with preserved average wages, starting January 1, 2027. This measure is part of a draft presidential decree on pension system reform. The proposal also includes changes for self-employed individuals and the cancellation of social tax benefits.

item.title: Tashkent Hosts International Business Forum for Regional Cooperation
item.description: Tashkent served as a venue for an international business forum within the "International Leadership Awards" project. Entrepreneurs from Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan, Azerbaijan, Turkey, France, and Kyrgyzstan shared experiences and discussed future cooperation in various sectors including energy and tourism.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan proposes restricting children's night access to anti-cafes
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is considering a bill to limit children's night access to anti-cafes and anti-cinemas without parents. The Ministry of Labor suggests this is due to risks of crimes against minors and substance abuse. The bill aims to include these venues in places with restricted night access for children, as they may not fall under current regulations.

item.title: Uzbekistan Plans Pension System Reforms, Expanding Funded Pensions by 2027
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to reform its pension system and expand funded pensions by 2027. A draft presidential decree proposes increasing the calculation period for pensions from five to twenty years of salary history. It also introduces a mechanism to exclude 10% of a citizen's lowest earnings from pension calculations.

item.title: Tajikistan and South Korea Sign Industrial and Technology Cooperation Agreements in Seoul
item.description: During the first C5+1 ministerial meeting, Tajikistan and South Korea signed a Memorandum of Understanding on industrial cooperation and supply chains. The agreement aims to boost industrial infrastructure, trade, investment, critical mineral extraction, AI, and smart manufacturing technologies.

item.title: Uzbek President Meets with South Korean Prime Minister in Seoul to Strengthen Strategic Partnership
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev met with South Korean Prime Minister Han Duck-soo in Seoul. They discussed strengthening their special strategic partnership in trade, investment, technology, and transport-logistics, focusing on innovation, digital economy, and critical mineral processing.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Launches "One Health" Project to Address Complex Risks
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has officially launched its component of the "One Health" initiative in Bishkek. The project aims to address complex risks, including infections, antimicrobial resistance, and climate change, by investing in biosecurity for economic benefit. The initiative involves regional governments and international organizations.
